newsitem.title: CANADA: World Wide to produce Kazakhstan uranium.
newsitem.headline: World Wide to produce Kazakhstan uranium.

text.p: World Wide Minerals Ltd said on Tuesday it has decided to take over management of the Tselinny uranium mining project in Kazakhstan and prepare the project for production.
Tselinny is a state-owned mining company with uranium mining and processing facilities in north-central Kazakhstan.
World Wide said in a statement it has secured the exclusive right to manage Tselinny with an option to purchase a 90 percent interest.
The company said a five-month due diligence review has shown Tselinny can be a viable uranium producer.
The Tselinny uranium assets include several underground mines with estimated reserves of 75 million tonnes of ore with an average grade of 0.12 percent uranium, the company said.
The company plans to develop a geological and mining plan to increase the grade to at least 10 million tonnes at a mining grade of 0.35 percent to 0.40 percent uranium.

The uranium processing mill has a design capacity of two million tonnes a year of ore. The company expects initial production to start in the first quarter of 1997 with maximum production to start within 18 months.
